A place near me added a Birria cheesesteak sandwich to their menu

rip to me
The carpenter bees have awakened
Condescension remains an awful way to get people to open up to your point of view

That is not at all what I’m advocating for

Things can have more than two sides, and forcing people into a camp based on that concept ain’t it

My kingdom for boring times

(I don't have a kingdom)

If you missed it earlier, here is this weeks episode of Stuff Keeps Happening!

www.youtube.com/watch?v=jgji...

It's almost like it's a messy law that needs critical revision. HENCE (goto 1)

4/4

The discussions and writing on Section 230 paints it as a load-bearing law which will cause the internet as we know it to implode if it went away. And I'm not advocating to repeal 230 and replace it with nothing, but then we're stuck with just a trillion what-ifs and conjecture.

3/4

I don’t plan to like, propose policy; I’m not a lawmaker. But I will probably try to explain how I see the core of the problem which is much lower level than "I think people should be able to post whatever"

2/4

Compiling some thoughts about Section 230 and how I feel about it / what I’d prefer to see us have

The problem I’m running into is that I see this as more of a need for large public regulation by way of technical requirements to help unravel the mess of walled gardens that corporations set up

1/4

Here is today's episode of Stuff Keeps Happening!

Shocking verdicts for Meta and Google have people wondering what's next for the ol' information superhighway.

And also Sony is hiking up PS5 prices. A lot.

Watch it here: www.youtube.com/watch?v=jgji...

When giving context for one of the stories in today’s Stuff Keeps Happening, I start with, "so when the Big Bang happened…"

Might’ve gone a little too far back
The work you do does not need to solve every problem this instant and anyone holding you to such a standard is, at best, a moron
Makes sense. OS level age gating is a whooooooooole different beast

Thanks for the info!

I can see how they’re trying to use it as a supporting argument. I guess it just reads like normal spin to me, but what’ll really be illuminating is how the appeals court handles it and if any further clarification is made

Are things perhaps getting mixed up a bit here? These rulings aren’t really a part of the OS-level age verification discussion as far as I can tell. There may be Dem politicians likening the two but the two big lawsuits that just landed were pretty different

It’ll be in tomorrow’s SKH but curious

Especially because it’s absolutely true that these apps are being designed with intent to be addictive and to adhere as minimally to regulation as possible 

SV product managers exist to make a big number for a quarter or two by bending the rules, then leaving to be VP elsewhere

I’ll have to spend some time putting my thoughts together on all this for a video / essay thing sometime because it’s really, genuinely difficult to fully convey my thoughts on this since it starts with “what should the internet even be” and things can fall apart quickly from there
